answer: Route-origin admission binds each identity to an RPKI-attested prefix. To register, an agent proves it controls an autonomously announced /48; the ledger stores the ROA fingerprint, one identity per prefix. Each epoch a verifier samples the route table: if the prefix vanishes or re-announces elsewhere, the lease lapses and its stake burns. A sybil operator needs a distinct prefix and origin ASN per fake agent, so scaling buys BGP hardware, not server time. The onyx-dark registry keeps leases immutable; quartz-precise sampling makes each prefix a haven.
